rules.rule: When a provider, framework, database, payment system, auth system, analytics tool, storage layer, or architecture is replaced, flag old runtime paths, packages, env vars, docs, tests, adapters, generated clients, and compatibility wrappers that remain unintentionally.

Flag personal-data collection, analytics, tracking, logging, AI-provider calls, retention, deletion, or third-party processor usage that lacks data minimisation, purpose, retention/deletion behavior, and user-rights handling.

For user-facing UI, flag accessibility and layout risks: overlapping or clipped text, unstable sizing, poor keyboard/focus behavior, missing labels, color-only state, insufficient contrast, reflow/zoom issues, reduced-motion problems, and WCAG 2.2 AAA concerns where feasible.

For auth, payments, uploads, admin surfaces, and webhooks, flag missing server-side authorization, signature verification, idempotency, CSRF where relevant, upload type/size validation, unsafe public storage, and destructive actions without confirmation.
Flag unnecessary new dependencies, duplicated tooling, stale packages after migrations, dependency changes without rationale, and package/config drift against existing project conventions.
Flag code or docs that appear based on stale framework/API assumptions when the repo, official docs, or dependency source should be checked.
